module_intro: Subtopics: IRL / ERL, Relative Equal Highs & Lows, Liquidity Hierarchy, Draw on Liquidity, Delivery Sequence, Voids.
prerequisites_stated_in_text: Advanced Modules 1--2 and the Intermediate volume. Liquidity is no longer treated as a list of pools; it is treated as the ranked set of objectives that define and constrain every delivery narrative.
module_objectives: Rank liquidity pools by timeframe significance (short-term, intermediate-term, long-term).
Distinguish relative equal highs/lows from ordinary swing points and state their role in engineering.
Map Internal Range Liquidity and External Range Liquidity to the controlling dealing range (Module 2).
State a precise Draw on Liquidity for any active narrative and defend why that pool ranks above alternatives.
Describe a liquidity delivery sequence from origin pool to target pool, including intermediate pools.
Recognise liquidity voids and their relationship to imbalance and rebalancing.
Identify opposing liquidity and the conditions under which it becomes the new Draw on Liquidity.
Internal Range Liquidity (IRL) sits inside the range boundaries - internal swings, internal equal highs/lows, and imbalances (FVGs) formed within the range.
External Range Liquidity (ERL) sits outside the range boundaries - above the range high and below the range low.
The pool's location (price or structural reference),
Whether it is IRL or ERL relative to the controlling range,
Why it outranks alternative pools given the higher-timeframe delivery narrative.
Long-term untested external liquidity that aligns with the higher-timeframe delivery narrative.
Intermediate-term external or strong internal liquidity that sits in the direction of the narrative.
Relative equal highs/lows that have not been raided and that sit on the path to the higher-timeframe objective.
Short-term session liquidity used for conditioning and entry timing.
Already-raided pools (lower priority unless a second pass is part of the narrative).

concepts.name: Liquidity as the Objective of Delivery
concepts.definition: Module 1 established that price is delivered from one liquidity pool to another. Module 2 located that delivery inside nested dealing ranges. This module supplies the ranked map of the pools themselves. Without a clear hierarchy, every high and low competes for attention and the narrative dissolves into noise.

raw_sections.Core Distinction: Not every pool is equal. The algorithm (in ICT's framing) does not treat a five-minute equal high with the same urgency as a weekly swing high that has not been tested for months. Advanced practice begins by ranking.

raw_sections.Role in Delivery:
IRL typically supplies intermediate objectives and the PD arrays used during retracement phases. ERL typically supplies the terminal objective of a completed delivery leg that expands or leaves the range. A narrative that cannot state whether its current target is IRL or ERL is incomplete.

**Evidence Classification:** *A/B - IRL/ERL terminology and usage relative to the dealing range are ICT-supported.*

concepts.name: Relative Equal Highs and Relative Equal Lows
concepts.definition: Relative equal highs (or lows) are swing points that are not perfectly identical in price but are close enough that resting liquidity is expected to cluster at or just beyond them. ICT treats these as high-probability engineering targets because retail and systematic stops concentrate at obvious "double top / double bottom" style levels.

concepts.name: Timeframe Hierarchy of Liquidity
concepts.definition: Session extremes, 15-minute or 5-minute swing points, intraday equal highs/lows. These are the pools most frequently raided during kill zones. They condition lower-timeframe entries but rarely define the higher-timeframe Draw on Liquidity.

raw_sections.Short-Term Liquidity: Session extremes, 15-minute or 5-minute swing points, intraday equal highs/lows. These are the pools most frequently raided during kill zones. They condition lower-timeframe entries but rarely define the higher-timeframe Draw on Liquidity.
raw_sections.Intermediate-Term Liquidity: Daily extremes, prior day high/low, 4-hour or 1-hour structural points, daily equal highs/lows. These often serve as the daily delivery objective or as intermediate targets inside a weekly narrative.
raw_sections.Long-Term Liquidity: Weekly and monthly extremes, multi-week swing points, untested weekly/monthly equal highs/lows. These are the pools that define macro delivery objectives. A weekly narrative that ignores long-term liquidity in favour of session noise is mis-specified.
raw_sections.Ranking Rule: When multiple pools are candidates, higher-timeframe pools outrank lower-timeframe pools for narrative authority. Lower-timeframe pools are used for conditioning and partial objectives.

concepts.name: Draw on Liquidity
concepts.definition: The Draw on Liquidity (DOL) is the specific pool that the current narrative expects price to seek next. It is not a vague direction; it is a named level or cluster (e.g., "buy-side liquidity above the 12 June weekly high" or "sell-side liquidity below the Asian range low").

concepts.name: Liquidity Delivery Sequence
concepts.definition: Origin pool (often opposing liquidity that is raided) -> displacement away from origin -> optional intermediate IRL targets -> terminal objective (often ERL or higher-timeframe pool). Retracement into PD arrays occurs after displacement and before or during continuation toward the terminal objective.

raw_sections.Opposing Liquidity: At every stage the opposite side of the market also holds liquidity. When a delivery leg fails, the opposing pool frequently becomes the new DOL. Recognition of opposing liquidity prevents surprise when a narrative reverses.

concepts.name: Liquidity Voids
concepts.definition: A liquidity void is an area of rapid price movement with little to no trading activity - the extreme form of imbalance. In ICT usage it is closely related to the Fair Value Gap / imbalance concept: price is expected, under certain conditions, to return and rebalance the void.
concepts.ict_specific_meaning: A liquidity void is an area of rapid price movement with little to no trading activity - the extreme form of imbalance. raw_sections.Delivery Role:
Voids left by displacement often become the retracement objectives (repricing) inside an ongoing delivery leg. They are not automatically reversal signals; they are inefficiencies that the algorithm may choose to rebalance before continuing.

**Evidence Classification:** *B/C - Liquidity void language appears in ICT teaching in connection with imbalances and rapid delivery; exact boundary with FVG terminology is sometimes fluid.*

concepts.name: Liquidity Hierarchy - Practical Ranking
concepts.definition:
When several pools compete, apply this order of consideration (all else equal):

- Long-term untested external liquidity that aligns with the higher-timeframe delivery narrative.

- Intermediate-term external or strong internal liquidity that sits in the direction of the narrative.

- Relative equal highs/lows that have not been raided and that sit on the path to the higher-timeframe objective.

- Short-term session liquidity used for conditioning and entry timing.

- Already-raided pools (lower priority unless a second pass is part of the narrative).

Hierarchy is always subordinate to the controlling delivery narrative and the controlling dealing range's premium/discount filter.

worked_narrative_examples.name: Worked Narrative - Liquidity Hierarchy in Action
worked_narrative_examples.definition:
Weekly delivery: seeking buy-side liquidity above the prior weekly high at 1.1200 (long-term ERL). Weekly range in discount.

Daily: prior day low at 1.0580 has been swept (intermediate SSL taken). Daily displacement higher leaves a FVG. Next daily internal buy-side pool sits at 1.0850; the weekly objective remains 1.1200.

Session: Asian range low swept in London; relative equal lows around 1.0610 also taken. New York retraces into the daily FVG.

DOL statement: "Primary Draw on Liquidity is the weekly buy-side pool above 1.1200. Intermediate objective is daily buy-side at 1.0850. Session sell-side has been satisfied and functions as the origin of the current daily delivery leg."

This hierarchy keeps the student from treating the session sweep as the entire story or from abandoning the weekly objective after a daily partial is reached.

failure_conditions.name: Failure Conditions
failure_conditions.definition:
Liquidity narrative fails when:

1027. The stated DOL is reached and price reverses with opposing displacement and MSS, promoting the opposing pool to new DOL.

1028. A higher-timeframe pool that was ignored suddenly becomes active and overrides the intermediate narrative.

1029. Repeated raids of the same pool without continuation suggest the pool is no longer the true objective.

Failure requires an explicit rewrite of the DOL and of the delivery narrative (Module 1), not a silent hope that the original pool will still be sought.

common_misinterpretations.name: Common Misinterpretations
common_misinterpretations.definition:
1030. Treating every swing high/low as equal in significance.

1031. Naming a direction ("bullish") without naming the concrete pool that is the Draw on Liquidity.

1032. Allowing short-term session liquidity to override long-term untested external liquidity.

1033. Assuming that once a pool is raided it can never be revisited (second passes occur).

1034. Confusing a liquidity void / FVG return with an automatic reversal of the higher-timeframe DOL.

evidence_summary.name: Evidence Summary
evidence_summary.definition:
Buy-side / sell-side liquidity, equal highs/lows, Draw on Liquidity, and the distinction between internal and external objectives relative to a range are core ICT. The timeframe ranking of liquidity (short / intermediate / long-term) is the consistent multi-timeframe extension of that teaching. Liquidity void language is used in connection with rapid delivery and imbalance. Community elaborations that assign fixed numerical priorities or mechanical scoring systems beyond ICT's demonstrations are classified as community interpretation.

***Source / Research note:** Primary orientation: ICT teaching on liquidity pools, equal highs/lows, Draw on Liquidity, and IRL/ERL relative to dealing ranges. Timeframe hierarchy is the operational synthesis required for advanced narrative construction. Secondary sources used only to locate and cross-reference primary themes.*

rules.statement: Timeframe hierarchy of liquidity: short-term (session extremes, 15-min/5-min swing points, intraday equal highs/lows -- raided during kill zones, condition LTF entries but rarely define HTF Draw on Liquidity); intermediate-term (daily extremes, prior day high/low, 4-hour/1-hour structural points, daily equal highs/lows -- serve as daily delivery objective or intermediate targets inside a weekly narrative); long-term (weekly/monthly extremes, multi-week swing points, untested weekly/monthly equal highs/lows -- define macro delivery objectives). Ranking rule: when multiple pools are candidates, higher-timeframe pools outrank lower-timeframe pools for narrative authority; lower-timeframe pools are used for conditioning and partial objectives.

A complete Draw on Liquidity (DOL) statement includes: (1) the pool's location (price or structural reference); (2) its timeframe significance (short/intermediate/long-term); (3) whether it is IRL or ERL relative to the controlling range; (4) why it outranks alternative pools given the higher-timeframe delivery narrative. Bias is incomplete without a DOL: 'Bullish' becomes 'bullish toward [named pool].'

Canonical liquidity delivery sequence: origin pool (often opposing liquidity that is raided) -> displacement away from origin -> optional intermediate IRL targets -> terminal objective (often ERL or higher-timeframe pool). Retracement into PD arrays occurs after displacement and before or during continuation toward the terminal objective. At every stage the opposite side of the market also holds liquidity; when a delivery leg fails, the opposing pool frequently becomes the new DOL.

Practical liquidity hierarchy ranking (all else equal), highest to lowest priority: (1) long-term untested external liquidity aligned with the HTF delivery narrative; (2) intermediate-term external or strong internal liquidity in the direction of the narrative; (3) relative equal highs/lows not yet raided that sit on the path to the HTF objective; (4) short-term session liquidity used for conditioning/entry timing; (5) already-raided pools (lower priority unless a second pass is part of the narrative). Hierarchy is always subordinate to the controlling delivery narrative and the controlling dealing range's premium/discount filter.

no_trade_conditions.statement: Liquidity narrative failure requires an explicit rewrite of the DOL and of the delivery narrative, not a silent hope that the original pool will still be sought. Failure occurs when: the stated DOL is reached and price reverses with opposing displacement and MSS (promoting the opposing pool to new DOL); a higher-timeframe pool that was ignored suddenly becomes active and overrides the intermediate narrative; repeated raids of the same pool without continuation suggest the pool is no longer the true objective.

key_terms: Draw on Liquidity (DOL) - the specific named pool the narrative expects price to seek next.
Internal Range Liquidity (IRL) - liquidity and imbalances inside the controlling dealing range.
External Range Liquidity (ERL) - liquidity outside the controlling dealing range boundaries.
Relative equal highs / lows - near-equal swing points that concentrate resting liquidity.
Short-term / Intermediate-term / Long-term liquidity - timeframe ranking of pools.
Liquidity void - area of rapid movement with little activity; related to imbalance / FVG.
Opposing liquidity - the pools on the opposite side of the current delivery direction.
Liquidity hierarchy - the ranked order of pools that governs narrative priority.
